root_cause.text: The mm/swap change incorrectly marked the global `swap_space` `struct address_space` as `__ro_after_init`, even though reclaim/error paths still modify its state (such as writeback error tracking via `errseq_set`/`__filemap_set_wb_err`) when swap preparation fails.
root_cause.evidence: The fix directly changes `swap_space` from `__ro_after_init` back to `__read_mostly` in `mm/swap.h` and `mm/swap_state.c`, and the commit message says commit `8b47299a411a` made swap address space read-only and caused a kernel panic with a stack trace ending in `errseq_set` and `__filemap_set_wb_err` when `arch_prepare_to_swap` returns failure under heavy memory pressure.

intent_record.intent_summary: Make `swap_space` writable after initialization by replacing `__ro_after_init` with `__read_mostly` to avoid incorrect read-only treatment of a mutable swap address_space.
intent_record.what: The declaration of the global variable `swap_space` in `linux/mm/swap.h` was changed from `extern struct address_space swap_space __ro_after_init;` to `extern struct address_space swap_space __read_mostly;`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this removes the expectation that `swap_space` becomes read-only after initialization and instead marks it as data that is mostly read. This allows the object to remain writable after init while still giving the compiler/linker placement hints for infrequent writes, preventing issues that would occur if later code needs to modify `swap_space`.

This is the defining statement that places swap_space in read-only-after-init storage even though its address_space fields are mutated later by swap preparation and error/writeback handling paths.
